title: This Animal Walks Across River Bottoms Holding Its Breath 6 Minutes

scenes.text: This animal crosses rivers by walking along the bottom.
A nine-banded armadillo can hold its breath for up to six minutes.
It can also swim by gulping air, which inflates its intestines like a life jacket.
And when it's startled, it can jump three or four feet straight up.
Then there are the babies. Every litter is four identical quadruplets, all from a single egg.
It's the only mammal known to always do that. A swimmer, a jumper, and a quadruplet maker.

description:
The nine-banded armadillo can hold its breath for up to six minutes and walk along the bottom of streams.
It can also inflate its intestines to float, jump three to four feet when startled, and it always gives birth to four identical young from a single egg.
Which armadillo power would you want? Comment below.
first_comment: Four identical babies from one egg, every single time. What animal should we cover next?
